hook.text: Aza Raskin invented infinite scroll in 2006. Years later, he called it one of his biggest regrets.

buildup.text: Before infinite scroll, pages ended. You hit 'next page' and had a moment to stop. The break was built in.

discovery.text: Infinite scroll removed the stopping cue. Content flows forever. The brain never gets a signal to quit.

twist.text: Raskin calculated infinite scroll wastes 200,000 human lifetimes daily. He now campaigns against his own creation.

climax.text: Every major platform adopted it. The design pattern that removes endings became the industry standard.

punchline.text: When there's no bottom, there's no reason to stop.

quiz.question: What design problem did infinite scroll create?
